articles.summary: LUCKNOW: In a dramatic development, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested senior Samajwadi Party leader and former MP Azam Khan outside Rampur
articles.body: LUCKNOW: In a dramatic development, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested senior Samajwadi Party leader and former MP Azam Khan outside Rampur district jail on Saturday, moments after he walked out following nearly 11 months in custody. His son, Abdullah Azam, was released and went home.ED officials questioned Khan outside the jail before taking him away in a vehicle.Sources in the agency said he had been arrested in connection with a 2019 Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). He is likely to be produced before a court in Ghaziabad, sources said.As ED officials questioned him, Khan reportedly had a heated exchange with them. Reacting emotionally to his arrest, he said, “What more can I say now? This is the punishment for being a Muslim. The mistake is that a Muslim built a university. That is our crime.”The ED team had reached Rampur jail before Khan's release. Around 24 CRPF personnel were also deployed outside the prison as the agency prepared to take him into custody. The arrest came amid a large gathering of Khan's supporters, who had assembled outside the jail to welcome him after his release.Khan and Abdullah had walked out of prison after the Allahabad High Court granted them bail and suspended their sentences in the dual PAN card case.The court passed the order on October 29, but declined to stay their convictions. articles.title: Wanted preacher Zakir Naik faces backlash for defending Taliban on Afghan girls' education
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik was criticised for defending access to education for women under Afghanistan's Taliban regime, which has
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik was criticised for defending access to education for women under Afghanistan's Taliban regime, which has notoriously restricted the equal rights of Afghan women.Naik, booked under India's stringent UAPA for terror-linked activities, said: "Everything that comes in the media is not true. The spokesperson of the Taliban said the situation there (in Afghanistan) is not very safe for women."The fugitive preacher said a Taliban ambassador assured him lesser restrictions when "safety is secured"."As far as I checked with the ambassador of the Taliban, they have women's education at all levels till Standard 6. So primary education is there for all females. Only higher education, because the environment is not safe, they are waiting until safety is secured," he said.Zakir Naik said that claims around Afghan women being denied higher education were "wrong and a misinformation"."All the other aspects of Islamic education, whether it be Quran or Sharia or PhD, they even have Sharia teachers. They may not have certain higher education of the Western world. To say that they don't have higher education is wrong. It's misinformation," he said."It is deeply troubling and disappointing to see an Islamic scholar of such global prominence as Dr. Zakir Naik rationalise the Taliban’s systematic exclusion of girls from education. Presenting an indefinite ban as a mere “postponement” and invoking a shortage of female teachers without explaining how that shortage can be addressed is not a credible defence. Such arguments risk legitimising the Taliban’s gender apartheid and lending religious credibility to a grave injustice," said Ziauddin Yousafzai, father of Malala Yousafzai.Mariam Solaimankhil, member of Afghanistan’s parliament in exile, said Zakir Naik should be ashamed, saying "some scholars suddenly lose their ability to reason"."According to Zakir Naik, Afghan girls aren’t banned from education. They’re just waiting for female teachers. The same female teachers the Taliban banned from working? Brilliant logic, Doctor! Apparently, when misogyny wears a turban, some scholars suddenly lose their ability to reason. Zakir Naik you should be ashamed," Solaimankhil said.Who's Zakir NaikZakir Naik, 58, is the founder of the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF). A doctor by profession, he is known for delivering inflammatory lectures in English, unlike many other Islamic preachers who use Urdu or Arabic. He was born on October 18, 1965, to Abdul Karim Naik and Roshan Naik in Mumbai.He attended Kishinchand Chellaram College and then studied medicine at the Topiwala National Medical College, where he obtained a Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS). articles.title: Unpaid taxes could jeopardise US green card applications, warn immigration lawyers
articles.summary: USCIS's tougher discretionary approach to adjustment of status (to a green card) puts applicants and in some cases, their financial sponsors under greater
articles.body: USCIS's tougher discretionary approach to adjustment of status (to a green card) puts applicants and in some cases, their financial sponsors under greater scrutiny. Tax compliance could also affect future citizenship applications.A policy memorandum issued by US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS). in May has reframed adjustment of status (AOS), which is the process through which eligible foreign nationals already in the US apply for permanent residence – it is now treated as a ‘discretionary benefit’. The policy calls for USCIS officers to weigh positive and negative factors in deciding whether an applicant merits approval.Unpaid taxes, unfiled returns and even partial payments under an agreed tax repayment plan could complicate an immigrant's application for a green card, immigration lawyers are warning. The implications could extend to both family-based and employment-based green-card applicants, as well as US citizens sponsoring relatives.Karin Wolman, a New York-based immigration attorney, says anyone preparing to apply for AOS whether family-based or employment-based should pay particular attention to their tax records before filing for adjustment of status."As the policy memo reframes AOS as a rare discretionary benefit, USCIS officers have been routinely denying cases in situations that used to be acceptable. One of these is where the applicant or sponsoring US citizen owes back taxes: if you haven’t filed a return yet because it’s under extension, or you are making partial payments under a payment plan with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) or the state, that can now result in denial of a green card application. Get your house in order, file the tax return and pay the balance owed. It is best if you can do so before filing the application, but definitely before the interview," she said.USCIS's discretionary framework requires officers to consider the totality of an applicant's circumstances. Compliance with tax laws and a record of paying taxes count in an applicant's favour, while failure to meet tax obligations can weigh against approval.The issue is also relevant where a sponsoring US citizen has outstanding tax liabilities. In family-based immigration cases, sponsors must generally submit an ‘Affidavit of Support’ in the required form, demonstrating that they meet the prescribed financial requirements. Tax returns and payment history are among the documents used to establish the sponsor's financial position.Tax history can matter at naturalisation tooTax compliance can have consequences even after an immigrant obtains permanent residence. Applicants seeking US citizenship through naturalisation must generally demonstrate good moral character.USCIS considers failure to pay taxes as a negative when assessing good moral character. Applicants with overdue federal, state or local taxes may be required to submit evidence that they have filed the necessary returns and entered into a repayment agreement with the relevant tax authority.Wolman also underlines the connection between tax compliance and naturalisation. "Timely payment of taxes is also a 'good moral character' factor when applying for naturalisation," she said.The tougher approach to adjustment of status is currently facing a legal challenge. A coalition of immigration advocacy organisations, unions and individual applicants filed a lawsuit against the Department of Homeland Security and USCIS in a district court in Massachusetts on Oct 5.The lawsuit states that the policy violates the Administrative Procedure Act, the Immigration and Nationality Act and constitutional due-process protections. The plaintiffs are seeking an injunction to block their implementation while the case is heard. As of date, the case remains pending, with no court order blocking the policies.You use AI every day. articles.title: 42-year-old Michigan man arrested for death threat to FBI director Kash Patel
articles.summary: A 42-year-old man from Michigan is arrested after threatening to kill FBI Director Kash Patel in a Facebook message. The case sheds light on growing threats against government officials as the FBI conducts further investigations into his background.
articles.body: A 42-year-old Michigan man has been arrested and charged with threatening to kill FBI Director Kash Patel, US Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr. announced.Anthony Daniel Palazzolo, of Chesterfield Township in Macomb County, was taken into custody on Friday following an investigation by the FBI. He faces a federal charge of transmitting threatening communications across state lines.According to the complaint, Palazzolo sent a Facebook message to an associate, identified in court documents as Victim-1, on October 8. He allegedly claimed to have “put a hit out” on the individual and added that Patel was a “dead mf too”.The complaint also details further threats allegedly made after FBI agents interviewed Palazzolo. A detention hearing has been scheduled for November 2.The charge carries a maximum sentence of five years in federal prison if he is convicted.The FBI's investigation also found that Palazzolo had a criminal record involving previous cases in Michigan, Texas and Florida. His reported history includes a 2018 charge related to falsely reporting a terrorist threat and a separate case involving an alleged fake bomb threat.Palazzolo's arrest follows another case involving threats against Patel's personal circle. Earlier this year, federal agents arrested 26-year-old Alden Welch Ruml of Massachusetts over alleged threatening emails sent to Patel's girlfriend, Alex Wilkins. articles.title: Animal testing in India: Why proposed new rules have sparked a fight over safeguards
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Animal testing remains an important part of pharmaceutical research, vaccine development and medical science in India.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Animal testing remains an important part of pharmaceutical research, vaccine development and medical science in India. But a proposed overhaul of the rules governing laboratory experiments has triggered a debate over a fundamental question: Can India streamline scientific research without weakening safeguards for animals?The draft Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (Control and Supervision of Experiment, Breeding and Trading of Laboratory Animals) Rules, 2026, issued by the Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA), proposes changes to how experiments are classified and approved. While it introduces a severity-based system for assessing animal suffering, animal welfare groups have raised concerns about reduced regulatory scrutiny, the use of certain animals and potential conflicts of interest in institutional approvals.The debate also comes at a time when advances in science are opening up alternatives to animal testing, including human cell-based studies, organoids, organ-on-chip technology and computer modelling. The question is whether India's regulatory framework is keeping pace with these developments.What are the proposed rules1. Severity-Based Classification: Experiments are categorized into four levels based on expected pain or distress: Mild, Moderate, Severe, Non-recovery2. Decentralized Approvals: An establishment's internal Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC) can directly approve mild and moderate experiments on any species. The central Committee for Control and Supervision of Experiments on Animals (CCSEA) retains approval authority for severe and non-recovery procedures, specifically for animals positioned above rodents and rabbits.3. Three Rs: Replacement, Reduction and Refinement. These involve using alternatives wherever possible, limiting the number of animals to what is scientifically necessary and improving procedures and care to minimise suffering.The proposed framework also lays down requirements for the registration of establishments, institutional ethics committees, veterinary supervision, trained personnel and animal-care facilities. Experiments may be undertaken for specified purposes, including basic and applied research, drug and food safety testing, disease research, environmental protection and species conservation.The sectors that use animals for researchAnimal experimentation is not limited to pharmaceutical companies. Dr Surat, Senior Program Director, Research and Toxicology Department, Humane World for Animals India, said it is carried out across pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, medical research institutions, universities, veterinary colleges and government laboratories.Animals are used in vaccine development and batch testing, food and feed safety assessments, disease research and studies evaluating the effectiveness of potential treatments. Tests may assess short-term and long-term toxicity, skin and eye irritation, carcinogenicity and reproductive toxicity.Mice and rats are among the most commonly used laboratory animals, followed by rabbits, guinea pigs, fish and birds. Non-human primates are also used in certain areas of research.However, the scale of animal experimentation in India remains difficult to establish. Dr Surat said that although an estimated 100 million to more than 115 million animals are used in experiments and research worldwide every year, India does not have an official national figure or a transparent public database recording annual animal use, deaths and reported violations.Dr Ramanuj Panda, founder and managing director of Gocarin, has called for a centralised reporting system that records the species used, severity of experiments, animal deaths and welfare complaints.What existing law saysAnimal experimentation in India is governed by the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. The law provides for the CCSEA to regulate experiments and ensure that animals are not subjected to unnecessary pain or suffering.Section 17 requires the committee to ensure that animals are not subjected to unnecessary pain or suffering before, during or after experiments. Section 18 authorises inspections of facilities and examination of relevant records. Section 19 allows the committee to prohibit experiments where the rules are not being followed, subject to the prescribed process.The proposed rules would change how approval responsibilities are distributed, particularly for experiments involving mild and moderate levels of suffering.Why are animal welfare groups concerned?One of the major concerns raised by animal welfare organisations relates to provisions allowing certain experiments involving protected wild animals, wild-caught animals and stray or feral domestic animals, subject to specified conditions and permissions.PETA India has flagged these provisions, arguing that capturing, handling, transporting and confining animals not bred for laboratory use can cause distress and disrupt their natural behaviour. It has also questioned the scientific reliability of using animals whose health, genetic background and environmental histories may be unknown.The organisation has raised concerns about the possibility of community dogs and cats being exposed to laboratory use. It has also referred to a CCSEA circular issued in 2022 that allowed the use of stray dogs in certain vaccine trials. The circular was withdrawn in 2023.Dr Noopur Jain, Science and Research Policy Advisor at PETA India, said: "India should be moving towards modern, human-relevant non-animal science, not making animal experimentation easier."PETA has also argued that the severity of an experiment, rather than the size or species of the animal, should determine the level of regulatory scrutiny.Could changes to approvals weaken oversight?Beyond the use of animals, the proposed shift towards institutional approvals has raised questions about independence and potential conflicts of interest.Dr Surat said five of the nine members of an IAEC belong to the same establishment seeking approval for an experiment, raising concerns about how independent research proposals may be assessed.The concern is that institutions could approve mild and moderate experiments involving a wider range of species without prior CCSEA clearance. This makes the role of independent members, veterinary supervision and clear scientific justification particularly important.Panda said streamlining approvals should not come at the cost of animal welfare. He called for meaningful participation by independent members in IAEC decisions, mandatory veterinary supervision, documented scientific justification and external reviews for experiments involving greater levels of suffering.The draft provides for inspections by designated nominees, including a socially aware member, at least twice a year. Separately, CCSEA inspection teams can inspect facilities to verify compliance.Dr Surat said facilities also undergo physical inspections for fresh registration and five-year renewals, while yearly mid-term inspections are mandated for large-animal research facilities.Another issue is whether India could become a destination for outsourced animal research.Dr Rukmini Jonnalagadda, founder and chief scientific officer of ULQA Scientific, Hyderabad, referred to an October 2026 investigation by Irish publication The Journal, which found that Irish universities had commissioned animal experiments at overseas laboratories, including in India.The University of Galway disclosed payments of €102,174 to an Indian organisation, Presude Lifesciences, for overseas studies.Ireland's Health Products Regulatory Authority confirmed that it has no regulatory role over animal experiments conducted abroad. The investigation does not establish that the Indian studies violated local rules, but it raises questions about how institutions commissioning research overseas assess and monitor animal welfare standards.Are animal experiments always reliable predictors of human safety?Animal models can provide useful scientific information, but differences between species can limit how accurately they predict human responses. Animals and humans may process chemicals differently and have distinct genetic, metabolic, immune and physiological characteristics.Panda said animal research should not be treated as proof that a drug or treatment will be safe for people.One frequently cited example is the 2006 clinical trial of TGN1412, an antibody that had appeared safe in preclinical testing involving non-human primates. During the first human trial, all six healthy volunteers who received the antibody developed severe immune reactions.Dr Surat also pointed to gene therapy research for X-linked myotubular myopathy. Although the treatment showed promise in dog models, clinical trials in humans were associated with severe liver complications and deaths.He also cited safety concerns surrounding Sarepta Therapeutics' Elevidys gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, which received a boxed warning from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) over serious liver injury.These cases do not mean animal research has no scientific value. They highlight the limitations of relying on animal studies as the sole predictor of human safety, particularly in complex diseases and therapies.What alternatives are availableNew Approach Methodologies (NAMs) include cell-based tests, three-dimensional tissue cultures, organoids, organ-on-chip systems and computer-based models. These methods allow researchers to study aspects of human biology without relying on live animals at every stage of testing.Organoids are miniature structures grown from cells that mimic certain features of human organs, while organ-on-chip systems reproduce selected functions of organs. Computer models can also help predict how substances may behave in the human body.However, these methods cannot yet replicate every interaction between organs, the immune system and other biological processes in a whole organism. They are therefore being used alongside animal models in areas where complex biological interactions remain difficult to reproduce.India has taken some steps towards recognising alternatives. The New Drugs and Clinical Trials (Amendment) Rules, 2023, recognised methods such as cell-based assays, organ chips, microphysiological systems and computer modelling for relevant regulatory purposes.A government response to Parliament in 2026 highlighted support for 109 non-animal testing projects by the Indian Council of Medical Research across 71 institutions and laboratories.However, experts say wider adoption requires investment in infrastructure, training, validation and collaboration between researchers and regulators.What needs to change?Dr Surat argued that the draft rules should do more than classify experiments according to severity. India should consider stronger provisions to promote the development and validation of alternatives, including a requirement that animal procedures should not be undertaken where a recognised non-animal method is available.The proposed framework could be strengthened by requiring researchers to document their search for alternatives before seeking approval, publishing annual statistics on animal use and establishing a national centre to validate non-animal testing methods.Dr Surat also flagged ambiguity in the draft's definition of a "humane endpoint", the point at which an experiment should be stopped to prevent further suffering. The rules, the expert said, need to establish a clear and actionable response when an animal reaches that stage.Panda said experiments involving prolonged suffering should face strict scrutiny, with veterinary monitoring, appropriate pain relief and clearly defined humane endpoints. He added that a transition away from routine animal experimentation was possible in an increasing number of applications, but would require rigorous scientific validation and a clear regulatory pathway.Dr Surat also pointed to policy initiatives in the US, UK, European Union and China to advance human biology-based testing methods. India, the expert argued, would risk falling behind without comparable policy support and investment.The challenge is not simply to reduce the number of animals used in laboratories. It is to ensure that research is scientifically justified, animals are protected wherever experiments continue, and credible alternatives are developed and adopted wherever possible.As the government considers feedback on the draft rules, the central question remains whether the proposed framework can balance scientific research with stronger safeguards while creating a clearer path towards methods that are more relevant to human health.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No drones or artillery shells flying into your courtyard': Oleshky evacuees reach Ukraine after journey through Russia
articles.summary: Hundreds of residents from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-controlled territory after undertaking an extraordinary
articles.body: Hundreds of residents from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky have reached Ukrainian-controlled territory after undertaking an extraordinary journey through Crimea, Russia and Belarus under a temporary ceasefire.According to BBC, the evacuees arrived in Ukraine's Chernihiv region on Saturday after travelling for nearly 19 hours to escape the humanitarian crisis in their city.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the successful completion of the humanitarian operation, saying that all evacuated residents had crossed into Ukraine through the Chernihiv region.He said roads leading to Oleshky were cleared of mines during the temporary ceasefire, allowing humanitarian supplies to be delivered and residents requiring evacuation to be brought out.He also expressed hope that humanitarian access to Oleshky would continue and thanked the US and First Lady Melania Trump for their mediation efforts.The evacuation brought an emotional end to years of separation for several families. Relatives waited at the Belarus-Ukraine border to reunite with family members who had remained in Oleshky under Russian occupation.Among them was 19-year-old Liza Paliy, who had not seen her father for more than two-and-a-half years after he stayed behind when she, her mother and sister fled the city."We thought at that time that it would be a month, two maximum, and we would return, but unfortunately, two years have already passed," Liza told the Associated Press.Another evacuee, speaking to Reuters after reaching Gomel in Belarus, described the constant threat of attacks in Oleshky and why leaving had become unavoidable."Here, there are no drones or artillery shells flying right into your courtyard. Many times we were literally on a brink of death back there," the resident said, adding that large craters had appeared in their vegetable garden.Valera recalled how the prolonged isolation had pushed residents to the brink, with food becoming increasingly scarce and families relying on whatever they could grow in their gardens."There was no bread. Nothing," he told AFP, describing the struggle to find even basic food. He said residents planted vegetables and ate whatever was available to survive.Why did evacuees take such a long route to reach Ukraine?Despite Ukrainian military positions being only around 5 km from Oleshky, residents could not take a direct route into Ukrainian-controlled territory because of the active frontline, the Dnipro River and the danger posed by landmines and drone attacks. The city lies on the eastern bank of the river, opposite Kherson, which remains under Ukrainian control.Destroyed bridges and mined roads made crossing directly towards Ukrainian positions extremely dangerous. Independent attempts to escape had also resulted in casualties. According to the head of the exiled Oleshky City Military Administration, Tetiana Hasanenko, one person was killed and four others injured by landmines while trying to flee the area in September.The evacuation therefore required a carefully coordinated route through Russian-controlled territory before residents could return to Ukraine. Under the temporary ceasefire, designated roads leading out of Oleshky were cleared of mines. A convoy of 25 buses, accompanied by ambulances and humanitarian vehicles, entered the city on October 30. Residents were given a four-hour window to leave, until 14:00 local time.The residents first travelled by bus to Armyansk in occupied Crimea, before continuing to Anapa in Russia's Krasnodar region. From there, they boarded Russian government aircraft to Gomel in Belarus and finally travelled by bus across the border into Ukraine's Chernihiv region.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: She left behind her dream of a career in law to build a life in a Nepalese village, but at 25, her £300-a-month lifestyle has helped her buy a £170,000 home in Yorkshire
articles.summary: If you've ever dreamt about owning a home at a young age, you know seeing this dream through can take years of planning, financial commitments and
articles.body: If you've ever dreamt about owning a home at a young age, you know seeing this dream through can take years of planning, financial commitments and balancing your career alongside it all. If you're young, building your own home could mean balancing a lot. So, while this journey towards owning property takes a conventional route for some, others may find themselves arriving at it through circumstances they may never have imagined.As reported by The Sun, for 25-year-old Madeleine Jaye, it was a rather unconventional route. Her decision to move away from the life she had once planned brought her to an unexpected milestone, allowing her to purchase a £170,000 property in Yorkshire while spending much of her time in a small village in Nepal.Hailing from Nottingham, Madeleine had spent four years studying law at Sheffield, with ambitions of securing a position at a major law firm. However, a trip to Nepal introduced her to Ram, her now-husband, who fortuitously changed the course of her life. The two met during a momo cooking class while she was travelling in the country, and what began as an encounter during her travels eventually developed into a relationship that would see her divide her time between two very different parts of the world.Furthermore, according to the report, Madeleine has been living between Britain and Nepal since 2024, when she finished her legal studies. She now spends extended periods in a small village approximately 25 minutes from Pokhara, where she lives with Ram, away from the familiar conveniences of modern British households. Their home does not have hot water, a refrigerator or a washing machine, and the couple prepare their meals over an open fire, making everyday routines considerably different from those she might once have expected.A different approach to living and savingWhat makes Madeleine's story particularly interesting from a property perspective is the way her living arrangements have influenced her ability to save. While the couple's household in Nepal has considerably lower expenses than a typical British household, her financial circumstances are also shaped by the work she continues to undertake in the UK.Madeleine runs her own personal assistant business, providing live-in care and assistance. Her work involves placements in Britain that generally last between six and 12 weeks, with accommodation included, after which she takes a similar period away to spend time with her husband in Nepal. This arrangement allows her to continue earning in Britain without having to maintain the same level of everyday expenditure throughout the year.As reported by The Sun, Madeleine estimates that her monthly expenditure in Nepal is around £300 at most. Together, these circumstances have helped her keep her outgoings relatively modest while continuing to work for part of the year.Life beyond the comforts of a modern homeThe lower cost of living, however, comes with its own adjustments. Living close to the natural world means that the surrounding wildlife is not simply something encountered during an occasional trip outdoors. Madeleine has spoken about keeping goats and chickens indoors at night because of the threat posed by tigers, while several animals in the village, including two of their pet dogs, have been lost.The monsoon season brings another set of challenges, making the experience of rural living different from the quieter days the couple otherwise enjoy. Yet Madeleine has come to appreciate the rhythm of life in the village, where swimming, fishing, drinking tea and travelling into the mountains form part of their everyday activities. Speaking about her experience, Madeleine described how living in Nepal had brought her a sense of contentment she had not anticipated. "Spirituality is woven into everyday life," she said, adding that the experience had changed her in ways she had never expected.Rethinking what owning a home and building a life meanMadeleine's decision to move away from her original professional ambitions was also influenced by a deeply personal experience. After losing her father to cancer at the age of 54, she began reconsidering the importance she had once placed on career progression, financial success and the expectations that often accompany them. She has spoken about how his death made her realise that time was considerably more valuable than the conventional idea of success she had grown up with.But this does not mean she has forgotten her interest in pursuing law. She believes she may return to law one day, but for now, her work in Britain and her life in Nepal allow her to maintain a balance that she is comfortable with. Her mother, who travelled to Nepal for the couple's Hindu wedding in May 2026, has also been supportive of her decisions.Madeleine’s story of love, owning a home, and directing a new path in life stays with you long after you’ve known it. Rather than following a single route towards financial security, Madeleine has built a life around working in one country and spending much of her time in another. However, this arrangement, which is shaped by her lifestyle and employment, has allowed her to accomplish a property milestone.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Microsoft's ex-lawyer, and now Washington Governor, is angry with the company; says: I love the company, but 'what's up with ...'
articles.summary: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson is reportedly not happy with Microsoft.
articles.body: Washington Governor Bob Ferguson is reportedly not happy with Microsoft. According to a report by GeekWire, Ferguson took aim at Microsoft over a political action committee's ad campaign criticizing the State government, speaking during what was intended to be an off-the-record business summit. Leaked audio obtained from the Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce’s Regional Leadership Conference at the Suncadia resort shows Ferguson directly challenging the software giant. The audio was originally published by independent state politics newsletter The Washington Observer.At issue is an ad funded by Washington Needs to Compete, a PAC that state campaign finance records show has raised roughly $13.8 million -- including over $5 million directly from Microsoft, alongside contributions from CEO Satya Nadella, former CEO Steve Ballmer, and President Brad Smith. Other corporate donors include T-Mobile, F5, Alaska Airlines and Weyerhaeuser.The commercial reportedly targets the State capital, claiming that “Olympia is broken, spending more while you get less,” and features a line that particularly irked the governor: “In Washington, it used to be all you needed was an idea, a dream and the guts to chase it.”What Microsoft ad says that made Governor 'upset'As reported by GeekWire, Microsoft ad opens with a nod to “inventors in garages,” “mom-and-pop shops down Main Street” and farmers “feeding the world,” before declaring, “In Washington, it used to be all you needed was an idea, a dream and the guts to chase it.”Then it turns, says: "But today, Olympia is broken, spending more while you get less." Jobs are leaving, the ad says, and “it’s harder than ever to afford a home and raise a family.” The ad, however, does not name Ferguson or any legislation. It ends by saying Olympia needs to "quit wasting money, fix what’s broken and put Washington families first."What Washington Governor told Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of CommerceAccording to GeekWire, Ferguson repeated the words “it used to be” in disbelief before pressing the room of business and civic leaders. “What’s up with that?” Ferguson asked. “First, does anyone else in this room believe that? articles.title: Philadelphia professor arrested for blocking delivery robots, says she would do it again because she believes she has more rights than a robot
articles.summary: A 78-year-old retired professor in Philadelphia has vowed to continue protesting delivery robots after she was arrested for repeatedly standing in their
articles.body: A 78-year-old retired professor in Philadelphia has vowed to continue protesting delivery robots after she was arrested for repeatedly standing in their way, arguing that her actions were an exercise of free speech and a protest against technology taking over public spaces.Carolyn Marvin, a retired communications professor at the University of Pennsylvania, said blocking autonomous delivery robots had become a habit since the small, wheeled machines began operating on Philadelphia’s streets and sidewalks.October 14 was not the first time Marvin had placed herself in front of one of the robots. She would stop them for a few minutes as they travelled along the sidewalk carrying food orders.“I was under the impression that I had more rights than the robot did,” Marvin said to CNN in an inerview.The October 14 incident ended with her arrest. Marvin said she had been returning home after getting a flu shot when she encountered a delivery robot. She had a jar of enchilada sauce in one hand and chicken biryani takeout in the other when she stood in front of the machine, as she had done on previous occasions.The incident took place in a busy part of the city, and a larger-than-usual crowd gathered. Some people supported her, while others criticized her. Marvin suspects someone in the crowd eventually called the police.Officers handcuffed her, put her in a police vehicle and issued her a citation for disorderly conduct.Philadelphia police said they had responded to a report of “criminal mischief involving a delivery robot”. When officers arrived, they found a woman “who was refusing to allow a delivery robot to pass”, according to an email from the police department. Officers issued multiple commands asking her to move, but she refused to comply.Marvin said she never expected to be arrested because she believed she was not obstructing another person.“I wasn’t impeding any persons. I was impeding a machine,” she said.She described her actions as a symbolic protest against the problems associated with delivery robots, including the displacement of low-income delivery workers, the physical risks the machines could pose to people using sidewalks and privacy concerns arising from their built-in cameras.“I also think that I have a First Amendment right to protest the abuses of corporations in public space, in the same public space that the robots are occupying,” she said.Marvin said she had previously taken part in protests supporting civil rights and abortion rights, supporting Black Lives Matter and opposing the Gulf and Vietnam wars. She sees her campaign against delivery robots as an extension of the same impulse to make the government hear public concerns.She said blocking the machines had also led to conversations with passersby who wanted to know what she was doing. Most were supportive or curious.Marvin said her protest had a limited impact on customers, with an office worker’s lunch potentially delayed by around 15 minutes at most. She added that she did not have unlimited time to spend blocking robots and would do so for 10 or 15 minutes when it was “convenient and possible”.A friend summed up her arrest by telling her: “Well, you got a disorderly conduct charge for impeding capitalism.”Why delivery robots have legal protectionFollowing her arrest, Marvin learnt more about the legal framework governing autonomous delivery devices in Pennsylvania.In 2020, the state legislature passed a law classifying autonomous delivery robots, described in the legislation as “personal delivery devices”, as pedestrians rather than vehicles.The legislation was largely opposed by Democrats, labour unions and accessibility advocates, who argued that allowing delivery robots could threaten jobs and put children and pedestrians at risk. Republicans supported the measure, describing it as an exciting technological development.The law requires vehicles to yield to delivery robots at crosswalks, just as they would to pedestrians, John Mattiacci, a Philadelphia personal injury attorney told CNN.However, the machines are also required to give way to people and cyclists in pedestrian areas.“Personal delivery devices must yield to other pedestrians and pedalcyclists in a pedestrian area,” Mattiacci said.Uber Eats launched its autonomous delivery robot fleet in Philadelphia in March, making the city the fourth in which the company offered robot deliveries. The machines have not been welcomed by everyone. Videos from Philadelphia and other places have shown people sitting on, kicking and vandalising delivery robots.Marvin sees the growing presence of delivery robots as part of a wider trend in which technology and machines are increasingly occupying everyday spaces.“There’s a way in which we’ve surrendered the streets to cars long ago, and I don’t think we should surrender the sidewalks to machines,” she said.“Machines in general encroach on our lives,” she added. “Public space is the most visible place where they’re encroaching on our lives, but they’re going right up the ladder, and lots of people are interested in making that happen.”She said robots were a visible symbol of the wider spread of technology, including artificial intelligence and social media algorithms that influence the images and narratives people consume.Her protest, she said, helps make the issue visible and presents it in a way that might otherwise go unnoticed.Asked whether she planned to resume blocking delivery robots after her arrest, Marvin had a brief answer: “Oh yeah.”This time, however, she said she would keep an eye out for the police.You use AI every day. articles.body: The Sidemen Charity Match 2026 became one of the biggest livestreaming events of the year, bringing together some of the internet's most popular creators for a special football game. Held on April 18 at London's Wembley Stadium, the event attracted 90,000 fans, while millions more watched online. However, the biggest win of the day was not on the football pitch. The match ended in a 10-10 draw, with 20 goals scored between the two sides. Unlike previous matches, the Sidemen members were split between the two teams to make the contest more balanced.Jack Joseph managed Sidemen FC, while Callum "Calfreezy" Aire took charge of YouTube Allstars. English rapper and singer Tinie Tempah also entertained the crowd with a special half-time performance.Simon "Miniminter" Minter had another big moment as he received the Adidas Golden Boot trophy for scoring the most goals in the match. He also holds the record for scoring the most goals across the charity match series.The event raised £6,218,875 for Brightside and M7 Education. A live merchandise auction also helped raise money, allowing fans to buy special signed Sidemen items.Sidemen Charity Match 2026 attracts 2.26 million peak viewers during livestreamThe match was also a huge success online. articles.title: Strangled after drinks, body dumped in lake: Wife, 2 lovers kill husband in Telangana
articles.summary: KAMAREDDY: A woman and her two lovers allegedly murdered her husband and dumped his body in a lake to make the death appear accidental.
articles.body: KAMAREDDY: A woman and her two lovers allegedly murdered her husband and dumped his body in a lake to make the death appear accidental. Banswada police solved the case and arrested all three accused.According to news agency ANI, the victim was identified as Chakali, alias Gummadi Kashiram, 26, a daily-wage labourer from Hanmajipet village in Banswada mandal.Police said Kashiram was found dead on the night of October 23, 2026, at Pachera Cheruvu pond on the outskirts of Hanmajipet. Based on a complaint filed by his father, Chakali Bhumayya, Banswada police initially registered a case of suspicious death.However, during the investigation, the preliminary post-mortem report indicated that Kashiram had been murdered. Police subsequently reclassified the case under Section 103 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police intensified the investigation, examined the scene of the offence, recorded witness statements and relied on technical evidence.On October 30, acting on credible information, police apprehended three persons from Hanmajipet village. The accused were identified as Chintakindi Ramu (26), a daily-wage labourer; Pasupula Santhosh (25), a tractor driver; both residents of Hanmajipet; and Gummadi Savitha (25), wife of the deceased.During interrogation, the accused confessed to the crime.Police said Savitha was allegedly involved in relationships with Ramu and Santhosh and conspired with them to murder her husband.As part of the plan, the three took Kashiram out on the night of October 23 on the pretext of drinking alcohol. Once he was heavily intoxicated, Ramu allegedly strangled him with a nylon rope while Santhosh restrained his hands to prevent him from escaping.Later, they dumped the body in Panchera Cheruvu and tried to destroy the evidence.The police have seized mobile phones and other material used in the crime.Police registered a case under Sections 103 and 238, read with Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). articles.title: Several arrested outside US Embassy in London for supporting pro-Palestinian group
articles.summary: At least 48 people were arrested during a protest outside the US Embassy in London on Saturday in support of Palestine Action, a group banned by the UK
articles.body: At least 48 people were arrested during a protest outside the US Embassy in London on Saturday in support of Palestine Action, a group banned by the UK government as a terrorist organisation.London's Metropolitan Police said most of the arrests were related to people expressing support for a proscribed organisation.“Officers remain at the scene and are continuing to make arrests," the police said in a statement, the Associared Press reported.More than 100 people took part in the demonstration, with several holding placards reading, “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.” Some protesters applauded and chanted “free, free Palestine” as those arrested were taken to police vans.A separate vigil in support of Palestine Action was held outside the US Consulate in Edinburgh, Scotland. Demonstrators carried placards similar to those seen in London.No arrests were reported in Edinburgh. However, Police Scotland said it was investigating to identify people seen wearing T-shirts and holding banners expressing support for the proscribed organisation.“Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate," Police Scotland said.The protests came ahead of a November 4 hearing at the Supreme Court in an appeal against the UK government's decision to designate Palestine Action as a terrorist organisation.Supporters of the group have criticised the ban as draconian, arguing that it violates freedom of speech. Under UK law, membership in or support for a proscribed organisation is a criminal offence punishable by up to 14 years in prison.In August, the US government also announced sanctions against Palestine Action, designating it as a terrorist group.What is Palestine Action?Founded in 2020, Palestine Action aims to end UK military support for Israel. The group says it seeks "to stop genocide by disrupting corporate enablers of the Israeli military-industrial complex". Israel strongly denies accusations that it is committing genocide against Palestinians.The group has carried out direct-action protests targeting companies and facilities linked to Israel's defence industry.In 2024, its activists broke into a factory owned by Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems UK and damaged equipment using sledgehammers and crowbars.In June 2025, activists broke into a Royal Air Force base, sprayed red paint into the engines of two tanker aircraft and caused further damage with crowbars.You use AI every day. articles.title: NC faces revolt as 25 MLAs seek removal of ministers, Omar aide
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah faces a growing revolt within National Conference (NC), with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight
articles.body: SRINAGAR: J&K CM Omar Abdullah faces a growing revolt within National Conference (NC), with around 25 legislators demanding replacement of all eight cabinet ministers, including the deputy CM, within 15 days and removal of his close aide and political adviser Nasir Aslam Wani.At a meeting at NC MLA Qaiser Jamshaid Lone’s home Friday evening, legislators passed a resolution seeking a cabinet overhaul and wider consultations within the party before portfolios are allocated. Around 18 MLAs attended in person and seven joined online, according to a legislator who was present. NC has 41 MLAs in 90-member assembly and runs a coalition govt with six Congress, six independent and one CPM legislator.“So far there is no next step. The first step was a big step to bring democracy within the party,” the legislator said. The resolution sought removal of all eight ministers and Wani for the “larger good of the party”.NC provincial president for Kashmir Showkat Mir confirmed the meeting but played down its significance, saying it was not directed against the party. He said some senior legislators wanted an appointment with NC president Farooq Abdullah. “Everyone wants to become a minister but the CM can appoint only eight in UT set up,” Mir said, adding that 24 legislators could be accommodated in the cabinet if statehood was restored.Omar, 56, and his father Farooq Abdullah are in New Delhi, where the CM celebrated his wedding with journalist Nidhi Razdan. Sharing a photograph on social media, Omar wrote: “A new journey began yesterday.” On July 31, Supreme Court granted Omar a divorce after being informed that he and his estranged wife Payal Abdullah had settled their matrimonial dispute through mediation.The NC turmoil came as party MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi prepared to quit the party and surrender his Lok Sabha seat on Nov 3, accusing Omar and his ministers of betraying the party’s promises on restoration of Article 370 and protection of J&K’s rights.“The crown prince and his cabal treat J&K as an estate passed down through the family,” Mehdi wrote on X. He accused NC of seeking votes on promises to restore Article 370 and release prisoners, only to abandon them after assuming office.Mehdi will address people at Budgam on Nov 3, the death anniversary of his father Aga Syed Mehdi, a Congress politician and prominent Shiite cleric assassinated in a terrorist attack on Nov 3, 2000. Mehdi has been among Omar’s sharpest critics, accusing him of abandoning NC’s manifesto.The MLAs’ meeting followed Omar’s cabinet expansion last week, triggering open dissent, protests and allegations of internal bias in NC after four ministers were inducted, taking the cabinet’s strength to nine, including the CM. He dropped Satish Sharma, leaving only two ministers from Jammu region — deputy CM Surinder Choudhary and Javed Ahmed Rana.BJP has predicted a split in NC and collapse of Omar’s govt. “I am telling you there is unrest against the party brass. They are looking for an alternative. Govt will not remain and the party will not remain,” leader of opposition Sunil Sharma said. He described Omar as a “prince, who doesn’t want to listen to any legislator”.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lucknow ready for next tourism leap
articles.summary: Lucknow tourism surges with 2 crore footfalls in H1 2026; hotel arrivals and room supply rise, with MICE, medical tourism and new attractions driving growth.
articles.body: Lucknow’s tourism economy has entered an aggressive growth phase. In the first six months of 2026, Lucknow logged two crore tourist footfalls. Estimates suggest that the number is expected to surpass 8.2 crore by 2036, giving investors an important reason to become a part of this economically thriving destination. TOI – which has been witnessing Lucknow’s tourism sector growth since 1984 – looks at the rise:PERENNIAL APPEALLucknow is a fine mix of heritage, cuisine and convenience blended well into a cosmopolitan frame of mind. While the legacy buildings offer old-world charm, the sentiment always appears open to new trends.But this appeal, that peaks in the winter months, never goes overboard. A sense of balance prevails which calms down the heart and mind and creates an experience that lingers on like warm winter-sun-kind-of-memory.The best element of Lucknow’s appeal lies in the fact that it is driven by committed native and emotionally invested connoisseurs. Alongside, the city has no dearth of offerings to shoppers and those looking for leisure.Tourism officials say that hotel arrivals in Lucknow have gone up from 8.92 lakh in 2023 to 35.31 lakh in 2025.Projections are that Lucknow’s appeal as a tourism destination will take this number to around 92 lakh to 1.1 crore hotel arrivals by 2035.GASTRONOMIC MAGNETISMLakhnavi food isn’t just any meal – it is a phenomenon with distinct character defined by enigmatic processes, heart-warming presentation and comforting after-taste. The Unesco city of gastronomy tag has officially certified this charm while opening avenues for local ‘bawarchikhanas’.According to a Future Market Insights report (March 2026), India’s culinary tourism market is projected to grow from around Rs 1.3 lakh crore in 2026 to nearly Rs 5.6 lakh crore by 2036, with street-food tours and walking trails expected to remain key components of the market.DIGITAL DOMINANCELucknow’s legacy and life has millions of takers on social media. From forgotten havelis and old-city lanes to kebabs, chikankari and stories of its artisans, the city is being rediscovered through reels, photographs and digital storytelling.The scale is striking: the #Lucknow hashtag has crossed 1.8 million Instagram posts, while Lucknow-focused platforms have built audiences running into lakhs.Younger generation is documenting its lesser-known histories, food traditions and cultural memory, turning nostalgia into a contemporary, shareable experience.In 2026, UP Tourism officially joined the trend launching a campaign and inviting young people to create 60-second reels about their cities’ heritage, food, culture, traditions, hidden spots and local experiences and position them as cultural ambassadors.NEXT BIG LEAPTourism department officials say that MICE and medical tourism would emerge as the pillars of destination Lucknow’s next leg of growth.The ministry of tourism has identified Lucknow as an emerging destination, citing its convention infrastructure, hotels, connectivity and cultural appeal. A govt district export plan has also proposed a dedicated Lucknow MICE Bureau to promote meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions.The city’s growing events profile can translate into longer stays if conferences, exhibitions and weddings are linked with its food, heritage, shopping and cultural experiences.Medical tourism offers another promising avenue. Lucknow’s tertiary healthcare institutions, including KGMU, SGPGI and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences, draw patients from across India. articles.title: Telecom, power services restored in most cyclone-hit areas of Odisha
articles.summary: Odisha cyclone update: telecom restored in 20 Ganjam blocks; power restored to 97% of 40.91 lakh affected consumers across 17 districts, officials say.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Telecom connectivity had been restored in 20 blocks of Ganjam district, one of the worst-affected regions, by 5 pm on Saturday, the electronics and IT department said. On the other hand, power distribution companies reported restoration of electricity supply to more than 97% of consumers affected by the cyclone.The telecom service restoration drive was reviewed by electronics and IT minister Mukesh Mahaling and additional chief secretary Vishal Dev.Officials said BSNL and other telecom service providers have been directed to complete restoration across all affected locations by Sunday evening.“The department is coordinating with all service providers to ensure the earliest resumption of uninterrupted telecom services," an official statement said.According to the power utilities, electricity supply was restored to 39.74 lakh of the 40.91 lakh consumers impacted across 17 districts within two days of the cyclone’s landfall on Oct 28.The restoration effort involved more than 29,000 personnel deployed across the state to clear debris, replace damaged poles and lines, and restore feeders and substations. Power is back in 23 of Odisha’s 30 districts.Southern Odisha, particularly Ganjam and Gajapati districts, remains the focus of the restoration operations. Tata Power Southern Odisha Distribution Limited said it had restored supply to more than 16.7 lakh consumers, over 96% of those affected in eight districts, and was continuing work to reconnect the remaining consumers.The cyclone, which brought wind speeds of up to 150kmph and torrential rainfall exceeding 500mm in parts of southern Odisha, caused extensive damage to power and communication infrastructure.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bhubaneswar | Silver Rate in Bhubaneswar | Bank Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Public Holidays in Bhubaneswar | Petrol Price in Bhubaneswar | Diesel Price in Bhubaneswar | CNG Price in Bhubaneswar | LPG Price in BhubaneswarStay updated with the latest Bhubaneswar news. articles.title: Madurai corpn floats tender for fresh SWM contract
articles.summary: Madurai Corporation floats new Rs 270 crore solid waste management tender for 81 wards, starting Dec, with GPS-tracked collection, sweeping, MCC upkeep and 24x7 complaints.
articles.body: Madurai: With the contract for Madurai’s current private contractor for solid waste management coming to a close without being extended, and in a push to overhaul civic cleanliness and sanitation infrastructure, Madurai corporation has floated fresh tenders for a comprehensive Rs 270-crore end-to-end solid waste management project. The move follows mass complaints and unanimous demands by residents and councillors to stop using the contractor for waste management.The 18-month contract aims to streamline garbage collection, transportation, processing, and facility maintenance across 81 wards in the city and will come into effect in Dec. The project covers Zone 1, 2, 3, and 5 excluding Ward 84.The selected service provider will undertake door-to-door collection of waste segregated as wet, dry, sanitary and special care directly from households, commercial establishments, bus stands and municipal markets. Corporation sanitation workers will support the contractor selected in ward 84 and zone 4, and work together to boost cleanliness operations across the cityCollection vehicles will feature dedicated, colour-coded compartments for different waste streams and will be fitted with GPS tracking systems for real-time monitoring. Primary collection vehicles will have audio announcements to broadcast awareness messages regarding source segregation daily.The civic overhaul also includes daily manual and mechanical street sweeping, cleaning and garbage removal at bus stands and municipal markets, pruning of trees, cutting of overgrown branches, clearing of bushes along roadsides, and regular desilting of storm water drains. The agency will operate and maintain key municipal infrastructure, including transfer stations at Thathaneri and Kochadai and various micro composting centres (MCCs).The civic body promises heightened accountability through an integrated 24x7 complaint redressal system, closing operational grievances in six hours.“Anything would be an improvement on the mismanagement the current contractor is doing,“ said S Shankar, a resident, citing the lack of daily waste collection in around 75% of the city. However, social activist V P Manikandan said it was still possible for existing contractor Ourland to return. “There are very few contractors with the revenue needed to take over waste management for an entire city,” he said.A senior corporation official said the new tender will have far stricter checks and balances to ensure that the contractor is performing well. “Failure to meet expectations can result in immediate termination of the contract,” the official said. The tender calls upon the contractor to support an increased workforce of sanitation workers in fewer wards, as they will be supported by the corporation as well. “This will reduce the load on the workers and increase efficient waste clearing,” the official said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Madurai | Silver Rate in Madurai | Bank Holidays in Madurai | Public Holidays in Madurai | Madurai AQI | Weather in Madurai | Petrol Price in Madurai | Diesel Price in Madurai | CNG Price in Madurai | LPG Price in MaduraiStay updated with the latest Madurai news. articles.title: INTACH calls for water availability and wildfire prevention measures around Sambhajinagar forests
articles.summary: INTACH urges Sambhajinagar forest dept to create waterholes, restore sources and fire lines in Gautala, Ajanta ranges to tackle drought and prevent wildfires.
articles.body: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: Citing prevailing drought conditions and anticipated water scarcity, Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage (INTACH), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar chapter, has urged the forest department to take immediate water availability and wildfire prevention measures in forests around the district.In a representation submitted to forest department officials, INTACH co-convener Swapnil Joshi sought creation of new water holes and priority implementation of fire-line works in Gautala Wildlife Sanctuary, Ajanta forest ranges and plantation areas around Sarola, Mhaismal and Daulatabad.“Forest ranges are ecologically significant as they support diverse wildlife and bird species. Rapidly declining natural water resources and dry climatic conditions will cause acute water scarcity for wildlife during summer. This situation could force wild animals to venture into human settlements in search of drinking water and increase human-wildlife conflict,” Joshi said.INTACH requested the forest department to identify suitable locations for new waterholes, ponds and other water bodies, along with restoration, desilting and deepening of existing natural and artificial sources. It also recommended watershed management interventions such as small check dams, contour trenches, percolation structures and groundwater recharge measures. The organisation placed special emphasis on drinking water for wildlife at vulnerable locations, and on developing sustainable water harvesting facilities at plantation sites.Drawing attention to the increased risk of forest fires during prolonged dry spells, INTACH urged the department to prioritise planning, creation, clearing and maintenance of fire lines across vulnerable ranges to prevent the outbreak and spread of wildfires.“Such measures are essential to safeguard wildlife habitats, forest vegetation, biodiversity and settlements adjoining forests,” Joshi added.The organisation also proposed a joint site inspection with forest officials to identify priority locations, assess existing resources and formulate a timely conservation programme before summer 2027, along with a willingness to create public awareness for community participation initiatives, stating that forest and wildlife conservation is an integral part of heritage conservation.Chief conservator of forests for Marathwada, Pramod Chand Lakra, said the forest department is closely monitoring the drought situation and taking measures to protect wildlife.Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: Students set example of conservation at park clean-up drives in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru students and citizens join #IamBengaluru park clean-up drives at Jakkuru, JP Nagar Mini Forest and Doddakallasandra Lake Park.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Students and citizens continued to come together for Bengaluru’s neighbourhood parks Saturday under the Times Of India’s #IamBengaluru – Volunteer for Parks, presented by Multigen, in association with Kristu Jayanti University and supported by the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA).At Jakkuru Park, Jala Poshan led a de-weeding and cleaning activity, with more than 50 students from Kristu Jayanti University joining the drive. In JP Nagar Mini Forest, comprising Bhagat Singh Park and Rajguru Park, Youth for Seva led clean-up activities, including park-vicinity cleaning and a plogging drive. At Doddakallasandra Lake Park, YFS volunteers also took part in a plogging and de-weeding activity.The weekend’s participation reflected the growing involvement of young citizens in caring for Bengaluru’s shared spaces, seen as places for recreation, community and a break from the pace of city life.Sunny Gabriel, 3rd year, life sciences, Kristu Jayanti University, said, “We came to Jakkur Lake as a group of 40 students because keeping the surroundings healthy requires effort. Coming here early on a weekend is not always easy, but putting in that effort matters.”Arpita Priya, 3rd year, forensic science, Kristu Jayanti University, added: “Bengaluru is changing rapidly, making it increasingly important for citizens to care for the environment around them. This initiative gives students an opportunity to turn that concern into action, and I hope more people will come forward to volunteer at lakes and other public spaces.”B Sreenadh, software engineer, Cognizant; Nagawara resident, recalled, “I remember Bengaluru’s parks as much greener when I was growing up, but the city’s expansion is changing that landscape. We need citizens to give a few hours each week to protect our community parks.”Jayashree, homemaker, JP Nagar, said, “I had wanted to volunteer for parks and am glad to finally get the opportunity. Parks are used by children, youngsters and senior citizens every day, so keeping them clean is a way of welcoming everyone and encouraging healthier lifestyles. I love walking and running in parks, and they give me a lot of energy.”Ishan, Class 10, Team Evara, NPS Rajajinagar said he has always loved spending time in its parks. “Cleaning the park today made me happy, and I hope initiatives like #IamBengaluru can help bring Bengaluru back to how it used to be.”Nishanth Rao G, IT Employee, Bengaluru South resident, added, “I wanted to help make the park a clean, green and welcoming space where everyone can enjoy spending time. Parks should be places where people come to relax and connect with nature, not avoid because of litter and dirt. I wanted to do my part so that everyone who visit after us feels happy to be here.”Tisha, degree student, MESA College, said, “Lalbagh and Cubbon Park were among the first things I heard about when I came to Bengaluru, and they became part of how I experienced the city. articles.title: A youth boxing charity's executive director diverted a $50,000 donation linked to Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry's appearance on Ellen's show into his personal account
articles.summary: A former executive director of a youth boxing charity in Oakland, California, diverted a $50,000 donation presented during Stephen Curry and Ayesha
articles.body: A former executive director of a youth boxing charity in Oakland, California, diverted a $50,000 donation presented during Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry's appearance on The Ellen DeGeneres Show into his personal bank account. Howard Solomon, also known as Solomon Howard, was sentenced to 27 months in federal prison in September 2025 after pleading guilty to mail fraud and tax evasion. The donation was made to the East Oakland Boxing Association (EOBA) by a television studio in connection with a December 2019 episode featuring the Currys on Ellen's Greatest Night of Giveaways. Prosecutors said Solomon embezzled at least $549,000 from the organisation between 2017 and 2021, using charitable funds for personal expenses. He was also ordered to repay the charity and the Internal Revenue Service.How the $50,000 donation was divertedAccording to the US Department of Justice, EOBA received the $50,000 donation in October 2019. The contribution was connected to the Currys' appearance on The Ellen DeGeneres Show in December that year, during a segment called Ellen's Greatest Night of Giveaways.During the segment, Stephen and Ayesha Curry delivered various gifts to the organisation, including a $50,000 cheque from the show. Solomon deposited the donation into a personal bank account without informing the charity's board members or staff.The donation came from the television studio, not necessarily from the Currys personally. The Justice Department identified the studio as the donor and linked the gift to the couple's appearance on the programme.Who is Howard Solomon?Solomon served as executive director of the East Oakland Boxing Association from approximately late 2016 until 2021. His responsibilities included overseeing the organisation's daily operations, fundraising, programmes, staff and finances.He was an authorised signatory on the charity's Wells Fargo bank accounts. Prosecutors said he used this access to transfer organisational funds into accounts he controlled at other financial institutions. He also deposited charitable contributions into personal and business accounts without the organisation's authorisation.He embezzled at least $549,000 from the charityThe $50,000 donation was only one part of a wider embezzlement scheme. Solomon admitted to taking at least $549,000 from EOBA over several years.Prosecutors said he used the money for personal expenses unrelated to his role at the organisation. These included a Ford Explorer, a vacation rental and purchases made through Amazon.The Justice Department said Solomon used his position of trust to divert money intended for an organisation serving children and families in East Oakland. The funds were meant to support the charity's youth programmes rather than his personal spending.The charity provides boxing lessons and educational supportThe East Oakland Boxing Association is a non-profit organisation that serves children and families in East Oakland, California. Its programmes include after-school and summer activities, boxing lessons, coaching, tutoring, literacy support and internship opportunities for teenagers.Federal prosecutors said the embezzlement deprived young people, particularly those from low-income families, of resources intended to support their development. The case raised concerns about the impact of financial misconduct on community organisations that rely on donations to provide services.Solomon also evaded federal taxesThe case involved tax evasion in addition to the embezzlement. Solomon admitted that he failed to report the money he took from EOBA as income on his tax returns. He also misstated expenses associated with two businesses that he claimed had incurred losses.According to the Justice Department, his actions resulted in an estimated $287,185 in unpaid federal taxes. The tax offence formed a separate part of the case, and the court ordered restitution to the Internal Revenue Service as well as to the charity.He was sentenced to 27 months in federal prisonSolomon pleaded guilty to one count of mail fraud and one count of tax evasion on April 23, 2025. On September 24, 2025, US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers sentenced him to 27 months in federal prison.He was also ordered to pay $549,132.74 in restitution to the East Oakland Boxing Association and $287,185 to the Internal Revenue Service.
